title: Migrate stored runs to include archived_at
summary: Add a nullable timestamp to the local SQLite runs table without changing existing query behavior.
problemStatement: Run records cannot retain an archive timestamp; existing rows and queries must remain compatible after the schema upgrade.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An old-schema fixture retains all run IDs and query results, with archived_at NULL, after migration and reopening.
Repeated opening does not reapply the migration; a valid timestamp round-trips without modifying other fields.

architectureNotes: Keep the local SQLite store boundary and introduce one explicitly versioned migration; retain existing read defaults.
securityConsiderations: Validate timestamp values and use bound SQL parameters. Migration must not broaden database file permissions or expose stored run contents.
rollbackPlan: Stop writers, restore the pre-upgrade database backup, and reopen with the previous supported binary after verifying integrity.

tddDecision.rationale: Behavior change requires regression evidence first
Behavior change requires regression evidence first

testNames: old schema migration preserves rows and query behavior
migration is idempotent and timestamp round-trips

dataModelChanges: Add runs.archived_at TEXT NULL. Existing rows remain NULL; new values must be valid ISO-8601 timestamps.

functionalRequirements: Preserve existing rows and existing query results after migration.
sdd.proposedTestStrategy: Use real temporary SQLite fixtures: old schema migration, repeat opening, timestamp round trip, and rollback backup verification.
sdd.designProposal: Apply the approved schema-version migration transaction before opening the new projection. Add a nullable column without rewriting existing rows.
technicalConstraints: Linux local filesystem and the supported SQLite runtime.
Do not mutate application contracts or silently accept a future schema version.
apiDataContracts: runs.archived_at: TEXT NULL; accepted values are ISO-8601 timestamps.
Existing query defaults and run identifiers remain unchanged.
risksAndTradeoffs: An additive nullable column preserves readers but requires an explicit compatibility check for old writers.
Restoring a backup loses writes after the backup; stop writers for rollback.
sdd.migrationStrategy: Back up and verify the database; apply the additive migration atomically once; retain NULL for old rows; validate row counts and queries before enabling writers. On failure restore the verified backup.
